edbDesc: Electromagnetic radiation generated by the acceleration of ultrarelativistic (i.e., moving near the speed of light) charged particles through magnetic fields.
title: Synchrotron radiation
inventor: Frank Elder, Anatole Gurewitsch, Robert Langmuir and Herbert Pollock
description: Electrons whirled around a ring at nearly the speed of light throw off a brilliant beam of light and X-rays as they turn. A General Electric team saw the glow through the glass of their synchrotron in 1947; giant rings are now built just to make this light for imaging proteins, materials and engine parts.
effect: fast electrons bent by magnets give off intense light and X-rays
usedIn: Synchrotron light sources for protein crystallography
strength: A synchrotron beam is billions of times brighter than a hospital X-ray tube.
pickWhy: Needs particle accelerators, but they are buildable and the light does real work; Cyclotron Radiation (another batch) is the slow-electron variant and could merge here.
